1.22 Keep a bulk preview build cooperative

Prerequisites. Verify the existing Classic executable, PID and launch time; record that identity and its observed scheduler state. Keep the SDK owner and normal resource/closure protocol. A token reservation does not limit Adobe’s internal worker threads.

Procedure. On macOS, an operator can put that verified process into Darwin background scheduling during an unattended bulk build:

/usr/sbin/taskpolicy -b -p "$CLASSIC_PID"

The installed manual and Apple’s source document this process-policy operation and its inverse. Check the command’s return status and keep observing actual SDK callbacks. Apple taskpolicy manual, Apple implementation.

Verify. A disposable Python control lowered scheduler priority and restored it; applying the policy to the bound Classic process also lowered its observed priority while preview callbacks continued. These observations do not measure contention fairness or an eight-core ceiling.

Undo. After bulk work stops/completes, reverify the same process launch before returning it to normal scheduling:

/usr/sbin/taskpolicy -B -p "$CLASSIC_PID"

Record restoration when performed. A saved undo command is pending cleanup.

Limits. This changes scheduling, not core affinity, a CPU quota or an RSS cap. It does not settle native calls, release leases or authorize another build.
